attacks.claim: For new sign-ups, NOTICE_PREV is set to `phone` even though they had no prior phone channel. STOP, failure fallback and rollback all restore to it. CallNotify ends 2027-03-31 and its replacement is out of scope (LIBSYS-330), so after that date these patrons fall back to a dead channel and silently lose hold notices. This breaks the 'no patron may lose hold notices' constraint.
attacks.evidence: "new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`" vs. "The CallNotify contract ends 2027-03-31 and will not be renewed" and "what replaces calls ... (LIBSYS-330)" out of scope

attacks.claim: The rollback claim that post-launch enrollees end up on exactly their prior channel contradicts the NOTICE_PREV rule. New sign-ups are assigned `phone`, not whatever they actually had, such as email. Rollback and STOP can therefore trigger automated calls the patron never chose, or no channel at all after March 2027.
attacks.evidence: "Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before."

attacks.claim: The no-lost-notice guarantee depends entirely on one hand-written webhook receiver, but the plan has no recovery path if it fails. Koha treats a queued SMS as sent once the provider accepts it. If a callback is dropped, rejected, or the receiver is down, a patron who sent STOP or whose number is invalid stays on SMS and gets nothing. The receiver is also rate-limited, so the morning burst of ~1,000 texts and their status callbacks may be rejected. The plan has no callback retry or reconciliation job and no alert on an undelivered backlog or receiver errors.
attacks.evidence: "exposes a single rate-limited POST path"; "on an `undelivered`/`failed` status callback, the receiver queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel"; ABSENT: reconciliation, receiver health alerting, callback replay

attacks.claim: The receiver's listed DB grants (UPDATE/INSERT only) cannot do what it is specified to do. Matching patrons by SMS number, reading NOTICE_PREV, and re-queuing the same notice all need SELECT on borrowers, attributes and message_queue. Either the receiver will not work or the grants will be widened ad hoc. Replay protection (a timestamp check on the signature) is also not mentioned.
attacks.evidence: "dedicated DB user with UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`"

attacks.claim: The budget constraint rests on an unproven 50%/10% uptake assumption. The plan has only a spend alert at $450 and no hard cap or defined action. Confirmation texts, fallback re-sends on the previous channel, and multi-segment Spanish messages are not in the math.
attacks.evidence: "Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons"; "a provider spend alert fires at $450"

attacks.claim: Number ownership is not verified: a typo at the desk or an OPAC-entered number goes live, and the opt-in is not confirmed by a reply. The statement that nobody gets an unrequested text is overstated, and a wrong recipient learns that a hold is ready at the library.
attacks.evidence: "Nobody gets a text they did not ask for."; "staff set it at the desk when the patron asks and provides a mobile number"

attacks.claim: The Spanish template is stated to be GSM-7 and one segment. Accented characters such as á, í, ó and ú are not GSM-7, so a typical Spanish message would go as UCS-2 and split into multiple segments. That raises cost and could truncate the STOP text.
The week-3 pilot sends real SMS before 10DLC campaign approval (submitted Oct 20, 1–3 weeks). Unregistered traffic may be blocked. No contingency is given if approval slips past week 3 or 4.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: staff pilot" vs. "Public launch is gated on approval" with approval typical in 1–3 weeks
